hints: Notice this is disproportionation, the same element is both oxidised and reduced, so focus on which oxychlorine product forms.
Recall that cold, dilute $\text{NaOH}$ gives chlorate(I), $\text{ClO}^{-}$ where Cl is +1, while hot, concentrated $\text{NaOH}$ gives chlorate(V), $\text{ClO}_3^{-}$ where Cl is +5.
Think about the silver halide test colours, and link the $\text{Cl}^{-}$ ion with oxidation state -1 to its familiar precipitate with $\text{Ag}^{+}$.
walkthrough:
**Spot the disproportionation**

Chlorine starts at 0 in $\text{Cl}_2$. Going to -1 is reduction, going to +1 is oxidation. So $\text{Cl}_2$ is both oxidised and reduced.

This is called disproportionation.

**Choose cold dilute for +1**

There are two famous reactions of chlorine with alkali. Learn them as a pair.

Cold, dilute alkali gives chloride and chlorate(I):
$$\text{Cl}_2 + 2\text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{NaCl} + \text{NaClO} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
Here Cl is -1 in $\text{NaCl}$ and +1 in $\text{NaClO}$.

**Contrast with hot concentrated**

Hot, concentrated alkali pushes oxidation further to +5.
$$3\text{Cl}_2 + 6\text{NaOH} \rightarrow 5\text{NaCl} + \text{NaClO}_3 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
Here Cl is -1 and +5, so this does not match the question which asks for +1.

**Recall the colour of AgCl**

Chlorine in oxidation state -1 means chloride ion, $\text{Cl}^{-}$. With $\text{Ag}^{+}$ it forms silver chloride.
$$\text{Ag}^{+}(aq) + \text{Cl}^{-}(aq) \rightarrow \text{AgCl}(s)$$
$\text{AgCl}$ is a white solid. This pairs cold, dilute alkali with white.

options.A: Correct. Cold, dilute $\text{NaOH}$ gives $\text{Cl}^{-}$ (-1) and $\text{ClO}^{-}$ (+1), exactly the change described. The -1 salt $\text{AgCl}$ is white.
options.B: Conditions are right but colour is wrong. Yellow is a common mix-up with $\text{AgBr}$ (cream) or $\text{AgI}$ (yellow). $\text{AgCl}$ is definitely white.
options.C: Colour is right but conditions are wrong. Hot, concentrated alkali gives $\text{ClO}_3^{-}$ where Cl is +5, not +1. This is a classic trap if you forget the two different disproportionation products.
options.D: Both parts are wrong for this question. Hot, concentrated gives +5 not +1, and the chloride salt $\text{AgCl}$ is white not yellow.
